note: Written from the app and docs on 10 Nov 2026. Review before launch.

faq.q: What does URBANOVA do?
faq.a: It checks an urban design for heat problems. From your site, plan and planning rules it calculates indicators (green space, hard surface, shade, building coverage), finds design hotspots, suggests measured options with costs, compares designs and writes a report. Every value shows its source, method and limitations.

faq.q: What does URBANOVA not do?
faq.a: It does not predict future temperatures or comfort for a design, run CFD simulations, approve designs on behalf of an authority, or guarantee savings or health outcomes. It gives the direction of an effect and measured geometric changes.

faq.q: Can I analyse a plot of land before I have a design?
faq.a: Yes. Create the project with just a name and the location (a site boundary helps), confirm the location, then click 'Analyse this site now' on 1 · Site. The site analysis shows the land as it is today: the climate and hot days, surface temperature against the surroundings, vegetation, land cover, the surroundings, and how hot it feels outdoors in sun and in shade on a hot day. When you upload a design plan later, the full analysis adds design hotspots, options, costs, rule checks and comparisons.

faq.q: What does a significant trend mean?
faq.a: A trend is significant when it is very unlikely to be chance: the p-value (the chance of seeing a trend this strong if nothing were really changing) is below 0.05. The Trend Detective uses two tests, the t-test on a straight-line fit and the Mann-Kendall test, and shows the rate per decade with its 95 % confidence interval. If the interval does not include zero, the trend is significant.

faq.q: Why remove the seasonal cycle before testing a trend?
faq.a: Summers are always warmer and wetter seasons always wetter, so the month-to-month swing is much bigger than a slow trend and hides it. The detective subtracts each calendar month's usual value and tests what is left (the anomalies).

faq.q: Why do the two trend tests sometimes disagree?
faq.a: The t-test fits a straight line and can be pulled by a few extreme months; the Mann-Kendall test only asks whether later values tend to be higher or lower than earlier ones. When one says significant and the other does not, call it a likely trend that more years of data would confirm or rule out.

faq.q: Where does the Trend Detective's data come from?
faq.a: From NASA POWER, monthly from January 1981: air temperature, humidity, wind and soil wetness from the MERRA-2 reanalysis, rainfall corrected with satellite and gauge data (GPCP/GPM), and sunshine and clouds from CERES and GEWEX SRB satellite products. One value covers about 55 km, so it describes a region, not a street.

faq.q: What is the 'Long-term climate trends' panel in my analysis?
faq.a: Every analysis (with or without a design) tests whether the climate at the site has changed since 1981: daytime highs, mean and night temperatures, rainfall, humidity and sunshine, from NASA POWER. Each row gives the rate per decade with its 95 % range and a verdict: significant only when two statistical tests, both corrected for year-to-year persistence, agree. Click a row for the chart, or open it in the Trend Detective for more. It describes one ~55 km grid cell and the past, not a forecast.

faq.q: What are the 'Site trends inside the boundary'?
faq.a: The plot itself since 1984, from the Landsat satellites (30 m). Every year the clearest hot-season images are measured inside your site boundary and in the ring around it. Three trends are tested like the climate trends: the site's surface temperature, the site minus its surroundings (is the plot heating faster than its neighbourhood? the most reliable row) and the site's greenness (NDVI). The change maps on the map show where it changed; outlined pixels passed the false-discovery-rate test. The first run reads about 40 years of images and can take several minutes. It is surface temperature, not air temperature, and it is not a forecast.

faq.q: What do I need to start a project?
faq.a: Only a name and the site location. A site boundary, a design plan (GeoJSON or DXF), planning documents and unit rates can be added later and make more analyses possible.

faq.q: Can I try it with sample data?
faq.a: Yes. Use latitude 30.1200, longitude 31.8500 with the files in the samples folder (site boundary, baseline plan, alternative, planning conditions PDF and TEST rates), and tick 'This project uses synthetic or test data'.

faq.q: Why must I confirm the location?
faq.a: Climate and satellite data are fetched for the coordinates, so a wrong location gives results for the wrong place. Confirming it records that a person checked it.

faq.q: What does the synthetic data flag do?
faq.a: It marks a project that uses test or invented data. Every report page is then labelled synthetic, so it is never mistaken for a real assessment.

faq.q: Can I share a project with my team?
faq.a: Yes. The project owner can add members as editors or viewers. Viewers can read everything but not change inputs or post questions.

faq.q: Which file formats can I upload?
faq.a: Plans: GeoJSON or DXF. Planning documents: PDF with a text layer (English or Arabic). Unit rates: CSV. Optional raster data: GeoTIFF with its source, variable and unit. PDF and image plans are kept for reference only.

faq.q: What is an EPSG code?
faq.a: A number that names the coordinate system of a drawing, for example 32636 for UTM zone 36N (much of Egypt). DXF files and projected GeoJSON need it so the plan lands in the right place.

faq.q: Why are my DXF features flagged?
faq.a: A DXF without declared units could be in millimetres or metres. Those features are flagged until you confirm on the Inputs tab that the drawing is in metres.

faq.q: How are CAD layers turned into buildings, roads and trees?
faq.a: Known layer names are classified automatically. Unrecognised layers stay 'unclassified'; the AI can suggest a type, and you review each one.

faq.q: Where do the cost estimates come from?
faq.a: Only from the unit rates you enter or upload, with their source and date. URBANOVA never invents a price; without a rate a cost shows as 'price required'.

faq.q: Why isn't my rule applied?
faq.a: Rules found in documents are candidates until a person verifies them on the Planning rules tab. Only verified rules are checked, at most one per rule type.

faq.q: Can it read Arabic documents?
faq.a: Yes, PDFs with a text layer in English or Arabic. Scanned pages without text are not read (no OCR yet).

faq.q: Why is an analysis blocked?
faq.a: It is missing an input, for example a site boundary for site ratios, building heights for shade, or verified rules for planning checks. The Readiness tab lists exactly what is missing.

faq.q: How do I make an alternative design?
faq.a: On the Scenarios tab, create an alternative from the baseline and edit it on the map or import features. You can also apply a measured option from a hotspot card as a draft alternative and approve it.

faq.q: How long does a run take?
faq.a: With live data about 1–2 minutes per two designs, mostly fetching climate, OpenStreetMap and satellite data. The progress bars show each scenario.

faq.q: Why did a module say unavailable?
faq.a: A data provider could not be reached or had no data for the site. The run continues and reports that module as unavailable with the reason; a missing value is never shown as 0.

faq.q: What is a hotspot?
faq.a: A place on your design with a measured problem: a sun-exposed hard surface, a shade deficit, or a planning-rule violation. Each has a size, a severity, the metrics behind it, likely causes and measured options.

faq.q: Why is a severity capped at moderate?
faq.a: When a threshold or project-choice value behind it is still provisional (not approved), the severity is capped at moderate and labelled provisional.

faq.q: What is the difference between existing land and design values?
faq.a: Existing-land values describe today's site from satellite and climate observations. Design values are calculated from your plan; only design values change between designs.

faq.q: What do the AI labels mean?
faq.a: 'AI, checked by the grounding validator' means a model wrote the text and every number was checked against the run's results. 'Automatic answer' means the text was built directly from the results without AI.

faq.q: What data does the AI see?
faq.a: Summaries of your results (metric values, hotspots, options) and, for this assistant, your profile and your own projects' summaries. It never receives your passwords. AI can be switched off per project.

faq.q: Which assistant should I ask about my numbers?
faq.a: For detailed questions about one run's numbers, use the results chat at the bottom of the Results tab: it reads that run's records and checks every number. This help assistant is for guidance, the platform and plans.

faq.q: Why can't I compare these designs?
faq.a: Designs are comparable only when analysed with the same settings and data. Re-run all scenarios together on the Run analysis tab, then compare.

faq.q: Why is there no single best design?
faq.a: Without your priorities there is no fair winner, so URBANOVA shows the trade-offs. Give criteria weights (and a budget) to see the best design under your priorities.

faq.q: What is in the report?
faq.a: An executive summary, one section per design hotspot, the site context, the comparison and trade-offs, the recommended design and next steps, then technical appendices with every source and method.

faq.q: Why is my report labelled partial or synthetic?
faq.a: Partial means some analyses were limited or unavailable. Synthetic means the project uses test data or TEST prices.

faq.q: Where does the data come from?
faq.a: Climate from ERA5 (Open-Meteo) and NASA POWER, buildings and land use from OpenStreetMap, surface temperature and vegetation from Landsat and Sentinel-2, and land cover from ESA WorldCover, via the Microsoft Planetary Computer. Each dataset shows its licence and attribution.

faq.q: Are the results validated?
faq.a: The methods are checked against stations, real geometry and synthetic sites, but no real project has been validated yet and some thresholds are provisional. Results are for evaluation, not for statutory approval.

faq.q: Which subscription plan (Free, Pro, Team) should I choose, and what does it cost?
faq.a: The Free, Pro and Team plans differ in the number of projects, analysis runs, designs per run, team members and AI messages. Subscription prices are not announced yet. Open the Plans tab in this help panel, or ask the assistant to help you choose.

faq.q: I forgot my password.
faq.a: Password reset by email is not available in this version. Ask the administrator of your URBANOVA installation to help.
